title: Spectral presentation of a directed intersection of quasi-compact opens
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], $I$ a nonempty set, and $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ quasi-compact open subsets such that for every $i,j$ there exists $k$ with $U_k\subseteq U_i\cap U_j$. Put $E=\bigcap_iU_i$ with its subspace topology. For every $i_0\in I$, put $Y=U_{i_0}$ and let $J$ be the set of distinct members of $(U_i)$ contained in $Y$, ordered by $V\leq W$ if $W\subseteq V$. Then $J$ is a small nonempty directed poset with least element $Y$; every $U_i$ contains a member of $J$, and $E=\bigcap_{V\in J}V$. Each $V\in J$, with its open subscheme structure, is quasi-separated and its underlying space is spectral [def-weil-spectral-space]. For $V\leq W$, the inclusion $W\hookrightarrow V$ is spectral: the inverse image of every quasi-compact open in $V$ is quasi-compact. The inclusions $E\hookrightarrow V$ exhibit $E$ as the limit of this diagram in topological spaces: compatible tuples consist of one common point in $E$, and the subspace topology on $E$ is the coarsest topology making all projections continuous. These assertions hold even when $E$ or a member of the family is empty. For an arbitrary nonempty family of quasi-compact opens in $X$, the family of intersections indexed by nonempty finite subsets of the original index set (allowing an intersection to be the empty open subset) is again a family of quasi-compact opens, is directed by reverse inclusion, has the same total intersection, and contains each original member.

proof.text: Fix $i_0$ and set $Y=U_{i_0}$. The set $J=\{U_i:U_i\subseteq Y\}$ is a subset of the power set of the underlying set of $X$, hence small. Reverse inclusion is a partial order on these distinct subsets. We have $Y\in J$ and $Y\leq V$ for every $V\in J$. Given $V=U_i,W=U_j\in J$, choose $k$ with $U_k\subseteq U_i\cap U_j$. Then $U_k\in J$ is an upper bound of $V,W$. This proves nonemptiness, directedness and the least-element assertion without assuming any of these opens has a point.

source.place: equation-sections-of-intersection, paragraph reducing to one member; explicit set-index construction.

proof.text: For every original index $i$, directedness applied to $i,i_0$ gives a member $U_k\in J$ contained in $U_i$. Consequently membership in every member of $J$ implies membership in every $U_i$; the converse holds because each member of $J$ is an original open. Thus $E=\bigcap_{V\in J}V$. The inverse diagram is indexed by $J^{\mathrm{op}}$: the relation $V\leq W$ supplies the inclusion $W\hookrightarrow V$. Inclusions compose and have identity maps, so this is a diagram.

proof.text: For each indexed open V, use Mathlib Opens.isOpenEmbedding' and Topology.IsOpenEmbedding.quasiSeparatedSpace to inherit quasi-separatedness from X. The hypothesis hU supplies CompactSpace V.toScheme by isCompact_iff_compactSpace. The scheme instances T0Space, QuasiSober and PrespectralSpace from Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Properties, together with compactness and quasi-separatedness, construct SpectralSpace V.toScheme, as in lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral. This also works for the empty open.

source.place: Tag 094L, lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-spectral; Schemes Tag 01KO, lemma-characterize-quasi-separated, for restriction to an open subscheme.

proof.text: For an inclusion g : V → W, Mathlib Opens.isOpenEmbedding_of_le gives an open embedding. Its range is compact, since V is compact, and open. Quasi-separatedness of W makes K ∩ range g compact for every compact open K of W, by Mathlib IsCompact.inter_of_isOpen. The embedding compactness equivalence and image_preimage_eq_inter_range identify this with compactness of g inverse image K. Together with continuity this proves IsSpectralMap g.

proof.text: For a compatible tuple $(x_V)_{V\in J}$, compatibility with $V\hookrightarrow Y$ says each $x_V$ is the same underlying point as $x_Y$. This point belongs to every $V$, hence to $E$. Conversely every point of $E$ gives that tuple. Each projection $E\hookrightarrow V$ is continuous by the subspace definition. Moreover any open of $E$ is $E\cap O$ for $O$ open in $X$, and is the inverse image under $E\hookrightarrow Y$ of $Y\cap O$. Thus the subspace topology is precisely the coarsest topology making all projections continuous. Explicitly, for any space $T$ and compatible continuous maps $f_V:T\to V$, define $f(t)=f_Y(t)\in E$ using compatibility. For an open $E\cap O$, its inverse image is $f_Y^{-1}(Y\cap O)$, which is open; hence $f$ is continuous, factors every $f_V$, and is unique because its underlying point is prescribed by $f_Y$. This proves the limit universal property, also if $E$ is empty: a cone with nonempty $T$ would supply an impossible compatible tuple at each point of $T$.

source.place: Tag 0A31, lemma-make-spectral-space, proof of assertion (b), universal-property sentence expanded explicitly.

proof.text: For each nonempty finite set F, apply Mathlib Finset.inf'_induction to the predicate that an open is compact. The initial cases are hU, and the binary step is Mathlib IsCompact.inter_of_isOpen. Finset.inf'_union shows that F union G supplies a common refinement. Singleton infima are the original opens, proving occurrence of every original member. Membership in every finite intersection implies membership in every singleton; conversely Finset.inf'_induction on membership puts a point of every U_i in every finite intersection. Empty resulting opens and empty total intersections are allowed.
